explanation: Binary digits stand for 1, 2, 4, 8 and so on, doubling from the right. So 101 means one 4, no 2 and one 1, which makes 5.

claims.text: The binary numeral 101 equals 5 in decimal.
In decimal, binary 11 is 3 and binary 111 is 7, and binary 101 is not one hundred and one.
Binary place values, from the right, are 1, 2, 4, 8 and so on, doubling each time.
